control_flow: avoidWalls: if the right light is below 60 %, check the obstacles; otherwise call driveInTheDark.
If the right light is below 60 %: if the front sensor sees something, turn left 15°; else if the left sensor sees something, turn right 15°; else call driveInTheDark.
driveInTheDark: if the left light is below 70 %, drive forward at 30 %; otherwise call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if the front sensor sees something, stop; otherwise call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; otherwise curve right.
The decisions are nested: D2 is inside D1's dim branch; D3 is reached from both branches; D4 follows D3's else; D5 follows D4's else.

scenarios.coded_response: It stops, and stops again as long as the wall is in front of it.

scenarios.trigger: The front obstacle sensor sees the wall.
scenarios.title: Stops at a wall in the open

scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stops in front of the wall without touching it.

scenarios.coded_response: It curves left on black and right off the line.
scenarios.initial_condition: On a black line in bright light, with nothing ahead.
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker sees black, then the white floor, again and again.
scenarios.title: Follows the black line
assumptions: You didn't say where the line goes: the end of the line is where it should get to.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line to its end.

uncertainties: Your sentence only says not to hit tunnel walls: what the robot should do outside a tunnel comes from the program alone.
In a bend the wall may be seen by the left sensor, by the front sensor, or by both: which of the two turns happens first is uncertain.
Near a tunnel's opening the light is above the thresholds, so the robot switches to its tunnel behaviour a few centimetres inside.
Without a line the robot curves right without end: to reach a tunnel it needs a line under it on the way.
